text: EXPLAIN ANALYZE tells you everything about one query you already suspect is slow. It doesn't tell you which query out of thousands you should look at first. pg_stat_statements is PostgreSQL's answer to that, the same role SQL Server's Query Store plays.

It requires a restart to load, because it's listed in shared_preload_libraries, then gets created as an extension inside the database. From there, every query gets tracked, aggregated by normalized text so literal values don't create separate entries.

Sort by total_exec_time to find queries costing the most cumulative server time — a query run 100,000 times at 2ms each can cost more than one slow query run once. Sort by mean_exec_time instead to find individually slow queries.

This is the measure step from the tuning methodology, applied server-wide — find the worst offender here, then take it into EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Next up: shared_buffers and the other key configuration parameters that shape performance.
